newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia c.bank sells HRK131 mln bills, rates flat.
newsitem.headline: Croatia c.bank sells HRK131 mln bills, rates flat.

text.p: Croatia's central bank sold 131 million kuna in 35- and 91-day liquidity bills on Wednesday, compared to almost 300 million at the last regular auction.
The bank described the volume as "normal" for this week's liquidity in the banking sector, and said it was not likely to intervene in the money market before the week-end.
A new fortnightly reserve period starts next Monday.
The issued rates remained flat at 7.0 and 8.50 percent, respectively. But the bank turned down a three-million bid for 91-day paper because investor asked for a higher rate, an official told Reuters.
It had shaved 50 basis points off the 35- and 91-day rates two weeks ago.
Commercial banks are encouraged to invest their excess kuna into the bills, which can be used as collateral for Lombard loans and repo funds from the central bank in times of liquidity strains.
